title: Fixed-increment machine
statement: There is a deterministic Boolean Turing machine with no work tapes and four states, numbered $0$ through $3$, whose initial state is $0$. In state $0$, it moves right without output on true and remains in state $0$; on false it moves left into state $1$; on blank it halts without moving. In state $1$, it moves left while reading symbols, and on blank moves right into state $2$. In state $2$, it moves right, changing true to false and entering state $2$, or changing false to true and entering state $3$; on blank it halts. In state $3$, it moves right while preserving each scanned symbol and halts on blank.
hypotheses_covered: Transition behavior on each state and scanned-symbol case
